message.content:
Consider any one of the 52 ordinary cards. Look only at the relative order of this card and the two jokers. There are \(3! = 6\) equally likely relative orderings.

The ordinary card is strictly between the two jokers in exactly 2 of these 6 orderings:
\[
J_1,\ \text{card},\ J_2
\]
and
\[
J_2,\ \text{card},\ J_1.
\]
So for any fixed ordinary card, the probability that it lies strictly between the two jokers is
\[
\frac{2}{6}=\frac13.
\]

By linearity of expectation, the expected number of ordinary cards between the jokers is
\[
52 \cdot \frac13 = \frac{52}{3}.
\]

Thus the expected number is \(\frac{52}{3}\).

The answer is \(\frac{52}{3}\).
